summary: Track B worker wave: Haiku reconstructs planned batches, Sonnet spot-verifies, Haiku fixes once

layout_requests: net-transport/src/lc_android_socket.cpp (lines 39-41 and 119-140): drop the anonymous-namespace l_hostLC / l_countLC and the duplicate ThreadGetHostByNameProcessLC, and use the core-platform pair declared in core-platform/include/core-platform/w7_global_04.hpp. Its comment at lines 119-120 ('the binary's copy lives in core-platform, with its own cache') is wrong: the binary has one l_hostLC / l_countLC pair. Not edited here (other category).

net-transport/src/android_socket.cpp (g_host_cache / g_host_count, line 60): the XP host cache is the binary's single l_host / l_count pair, reached through l_host_ptr and l_count_ptr in 0x841ba8. Readers should use the core-platform pair from w7_global_04.hpp. Not edited here (other category).

Declare the request struct for threadGetHostByNameProcess (0x841ba8) and threadGetHostByNameProcessLC (0x89f8a0): busy-flag pointer at +0 and host name at +4 in the 32-bit layout. Both currently read those bytes by raw offset, which is not host-correct, so both stay partial until the struct is named.

Vendor-gameswf owner: declare the full tu_file member list (m_data, seven function pointers, m_error) where core-platform can see it (core-platform/include/core-platform/tb/tu_file.hpp declares no members). Until then file_opener (0x7a9954) allocates sizeof(gameswf::tu_file) = 1 on the host, which is a placeholder, and its row is partial.

core-platform has no IEvent, EvAcceleration, EvTouchScreenMove, EvTouchScreenPress or EventManager::Raise. Declaring them (vtables off_95B458, off_95C580, off_95C390, off_95C3A8; type ints 6, 5, 4 at +4) would let AccelerometerBase::moved and TouchScreenBase::ProcessEvents be completed. The EventManager stand-in in w7_console_01.hpp has only Attach and Detach.

deps/glitch_core.hpp now declares a minimal glitch::IEventReceiver (virtual dtor and onEvent). TouchScreenPS3 and TouchScreenWin32 derive from it at +0x1b4. At integration, replace it with the real glitch IEventReceiver when that category is unified. glitch-core-io's stand-in has no onEvent.

core-platform/include/core-platform/rss.hpp: class channel is a stand-in (read is empty). The real channel is net-session-online/include/net-session-online/channel.hpp, which reads through net-session-online/deps/slim_xml_node.hpp, a different slim::XmlNode from core-platform/slim_xml.hpp. Replace the stand-in with the real channel (and unify slim::XmlNode) in the engine unification wave, then rss::read (0x844050) can be reconstructed.

glitch::collada::SMatrix (rhs of operator*<float,SMatrix>, 0x6651a0): 16 floats read by index 0..15 from +0x00 (column-major); the flag byte at +0x40 is not read by this function. Declare it in the collada owner header so the operator can take it by type.

typed_attributes.hpp: CBinaryAttribute must derive from CStringAttribute. In the binary, CBinaryAttribute's D1 (0x5650dc) calls the CStringAttribute base destructor, and addStringAsBinary (0x56840c) builds a CStringAttribute and then writes the CBinaryAttribute vtable over it. The port declares CBinaryAttribute : IAttribute, so addStringAsBinary cannot be exact until this is changed.

attributes.hpp (IAttribute) and scalar_attributes.hpp (CEnumAttribute): the enumeration text slot. Vtable slot +0x80 (IAttribute::getEnum, base at 0x31d814 returns null) is compared with strcmp by the two choice forms (0x561f04, 0x562458), so the binary returns a char pointer there. The port declares getEnum() int, and CEnumAttribute::getEnum (0x560600) returns the word at +0x38, which the port names enumValue int. The CEnumAttribute constructor notes put the value text at +0x24, so the text slot needs resolving. The choice table (+0x3c, 24-byte entries per setEnum 0x5656c8) is also needed for setEnum, the two literal functions (0x564148, 0x5641ac) and the enumeration constructor (0x56706c).

Owner header file_system.hpp was edited directly for the batch: object size is 0x2c (createFileSystem operator new), so the obfuscation map is not a member of CFileSystem; getObfuscatedFileName and addObfuscationFileMap (0x56e064, 0x56e6dc) need their map located elsewhere (a global), not a member.

Integrator: CFileSystem() now sets referenceCounter to 0, as the original ctor does. createFileSystem therefore returns count 0. The existing tests/file_system_test.cpp calls created->drop() on that object, which no longer deletes it (one object leaked in that test, no failure). Consider changing that test to delete the object.

glitch::scene::CMeshBuffer (deps/glitch_core_objects.hpp stand-in is empty; owner glitch-scene-collada-gui or glitch-video): needs vtable at +0x00, refcount at +0x04, vertex streams intrusive pointer at +0x14, an embedded CPrimitiveStream at +0x18 (24 bytes, see tb/cprimitivestream.hpp), and a flag byte at +0x34. Needed by loadMB (0x6b7c1c) and save(CMeshBuffer) (0x6b875c), which are partial stubs until this exists.

glitch::video::CVertexStreams (owner glitch-video/include/glitch-video/vertex_streams.hpp; the io stand-in in deps was extended with streams, field08 and count0c): the trailing block of 24 * count0c + 24 bytes after the entries (the end pointer at +0x10), and the flags word at +0x0e. Needed to store and write back the trailing vector pairs in loadVS (0x6b73d8), loadHeadersAndSkipData (0x6b6cac) and save(CVertexStreams) (0x6b7d84), which currently read or skip them and drop them. Also the allocate(mask) rule for the entry count, which the io code currently replaces with one entry per header.

glitch::video::IVideoDriver (deps stand-in is empty): buffer creation at vtable +0x78 (sret intrusive_ptr<IBuffer>, this=driver, type, usage, size, data, keep flag; loadPS passes type 1 usage 4, loadVS type 0 usage 4), and the texture manager at driver +0xe0 with getTexture(name) plus the texture id (+0x3c) and the texture string/name node layout used by toString and fromString (0x5787cc, 0x578670). Needed to replace the private IBuffer and the empty texture results.

glitch::video::CPrimitiveStream (tb/cprimitivestream.hpp, io-side view): the names of +0x0c and +0x10 (unk_0c, unk_10) are not identified; the glitch-video owner should confirm the 24-byte layout (buffer, offset, count, two words, index type u16 at +0x14, primitive type u16 at +0x16) and getPrimitiveCount at 0x5a0300.

io/stream_itr_loader.hpp SStreamItrLoader is 24 bytes (data +0x10, count +0x14, elementSize +0x16, stride +0x18), but the vector loadVS (0x6b73d8) walks has 64-byte elements with the count at +0x28 and the element size at +0x2c. Needed to implement the big-endian vertex element swap in loadVS; the big-endian path is partial until the owner's layout is confirmed.

glitch-core-io/include/glitch-core-io/io/scalar_attributes.hpp (CEnumAttribute): the listing of 0x56706c stores the value string at +0x24, the choice vector at +0x3c..+0x44 and the enum index at +0x38, which conflicts with CIntAttribute's value at +0x24. A layout decision is needed before the constructor and setEnum (vtable +0xf8) can be completed.

CustomFree (0x310440) is declared in core-platform/include/core-platform/memory.hpp and is not reachable from glitch-core-io's include set (check_tu uses only glitch-core-io and shared includes). Decide whether glitch-core-io gets its own declaration, so the intrusive_ptr release helpers for 0x310be8, 0x351e3c, 0x3522b8 and 0x35eb90 can call the destructor and then CustomFree instead of deleting.
IReadFile::read returns int (not void) so CMemoryReadFile::read and the readAsync pair can return the count. Overrides to change: CReadFile::read, CLimitReadFile::read, the test fakes.
IFileReadCallBack::read returns a success flag so CXMLReaderImpl<char>::readFile can free the buffer and fail on a short read. Override to change: CIrrXMLFileReadCallBack::read.

CLight stand-in in glitch-core-io/include/glitch-core-io/deps/glitch_core_objects.hpp: add the +0x50 node pointer and the +0x54 flag byte. With those fields and a Matrix4Pool global, the pool push in 0x5aa3c8 and 0x5bb650 can be written. Owner: glitch-video CLight.

SIDedCollection record layout is per instance and the template has one layout: SShaderParameterDef SIdValue is 8 bytes (int 1 at +0x00, u16 id at +0x04; getProperties returns SIdValue+0x00); CMaterialRenderer SIdValue is 12 bytes (word 0 at +0x00, int -1 at +0x04, u16 17 at +0x08, u16 id at +0x0a); ITexture SIdValue is 0x20 bytes with id at +0x1c. Needs an id-offset/record trait before the 0x5b9f64, 0x5b9f74, 0x5d7e34, 0x5d7e54, getProperties and SEntry rows can be reconstructed.

materialrenderermanager::SProperties::onRemove(record, collection, id) must run before the node erase in the CMaterialRenderer remove (0x5d9f74). The owner class needs a hook (or the Props type needs an onRemove member) for this.

SShaderParameterDef value type: a counted shared-string pointer at +0x00 (count at +0x00 of the data, released through glitch::core::detail::SSharedStringHeapEntry::SData::release at zero), u16 at +0x04, bytes at +0x06 and +0x07, ints at +0x08 and +0x0c. The SEntry copy, set, reset and the SEntry() default (0x5b9fb8, 0x5b9fe4, 0x5ba010, 0x5ba064, 0x5bc5c4, 0x5bc620) and the destructor (0x5bb520) need this type and SData.

CLight (boost::intrusive_ptr<CLight const> destructor 0x5b9118): the original CLight has its count at +0x00 (no IReferenceCounted base), a matrix pointer at +0x50 that returns to glitch::memory::Matrix4Pool when the byte at +0x54 is clear, and frees with LC_API_FREE_0. The port's deps CLight stand-in has none of these.

IAttributes (glitch-core-io/include/glitch-core-io/io/interfaces.hpp): declare the vtable slot +0x100 virtual used by IAttributes::getEnum<E_POLYGON_MODE> (0x5e09fc), and glitch::video::getStringsInternal, before the body can be written.

glitch::core::IdentityMatrix: declare the global (CMatrix4<float>, storage at 0x9f6570, flag byte at +0x40 = 0x9f65b0; symbol size 68) in an owner header with storage, so the GCC clone of getInverse at 0x663ce8 can forward to it.

SIDedCollection IShader instance: the mapped value is 8 bytes with int 0 at +0 and the u16 id at +4 (ctor 0x5e5490), not the ITexture layout (id at +0x1c) of shared/include/glitch-shared/sid_collection.hpp. Its removeAll (0x5e66d8) and SIdValue rows need a mapped-value parameter in the shared template.

STextureProperties and SShaderProperties: declare the records in their owner headers with sizes under 0x1c, so the getProperties instances (0x5e53dc, 0x5e53f0, 0x5e83e4, 0x5e83f8) can be completed. The shared template returns node+0x18 for them, which matches the original.

SIDedCollection ITexture SIdValue (0x5e85b4, 0x5e85f0): the shared template does not write the string self pointers at +0x10/+0x14 or int 39 at +0x18. Add them to the mapped value if the integrator accepts the layout.

CZipWriter (glitch-core-io/include/glitch-core-io/io/zip_writer.hpp): add the block pointer at +0x18 (freed by the destructor) and the central-directory buffers at +0x10..+0x20 that CZipWriter::close (0x6b4fec, currently skipped) needs. Unblocks the two destructors 0x6b5238 and 0x6b5288.

IReadFile::read (glitch-core-io/include/glitch-core-io/io/read_file.hpp, slot +0x0c): return the byte count as unsigned int instead of void. Needed by CLimitReadFile::read (0x6b44e8), which adds the count to position, and by the int return values of SStreamItrLoader::loadAndAdvance and SStreamItrWriter::writeAndAdvance.

SIDedCollection IShaderCode instance (glitch-core-io/include/glitch-core-io/core/sided_collection.hpp): the SIdValue id is the first field (node+0x18). getId (0x6e1ab4), removeAll (0x6e1f50) and the SIdValue ctor (0x6e08b0) all read it there. The glitch-shared template and the NOTES place it at +0x1c for the ITexture instance. Keep the layouts per instance when the templates are unified.

Pre-existing, not from this batch: tests/sided_collection_test.cpp does not link (undefined reference to glitch::IReferenceCounted::drop() const, pulled in by boost::intrusive_ptr_release). check_tu.sh --test fails on it before any of this batch's code runs.

Base chain for vox::DriverAndroid. The binary has DriverAndroid : DriverCallbackInterface : DriverInterface, with the callback base's Mutex at +0x04, active flag at +0x08, source counter at +0x0c (also the flags of each new source), source list sentinel at +0x10 and listener at +0x18. In the port, driver_callback.hpp declares DriverCallbackInterface with no base, and DriverAndroid derives only from DriverInterface, so the base counter, the source list, the protected _FillBuffer, and the base Init, SetDefaultParameter, constructor and destructor calls are unreachable. Integrator to decide the chain (for example DriverCallbackInterface : DriverInterface, then DriverAndroid : DriverCallbackInterface). This one change would unblock CreateDriverSource, the list unlink in DestroyDriverSource, the DoCallbackAT JNI fill, Init, and C1/C2/D0/D1/D2. Not changed here, since driver_callback.hpp is outside this batch.

JNI bridge decision. The JNI-dependent parts (GetEnv, the AudioTrack methods, the byte-array critical section, AttachCurrentThread) need a JNIEnv or stand-in. None exists in vox-audio, and the net-session-online deps stand-in is not reusable from here. Not added here, so those calls stay as partial notes. Also: vox-audio's CMake target does not link core-platform, so _GetTime (core-platform 0x862bf4) is replaced by a steady-clock helper, as vox_thread_object.cpp already does.

DriverInterface: the listing at 0x86e1a8 (KillEmitter, slot +0x48) calls the driver with the driver pointer alone, no second argument. The port's slot +0x48 is DestroyDriverSource(source) (DriverAndroid). The integrator should decide whether a no-argument slot +0x48 exists in the owner header, so KillEmitter can make that call.

DecoderCursorInterface: the track parameter block (cursor +0x04..+0x10: channels, sample rate, bits, length) is read by LoadDataSource (0x86b144), ConvertToRawSource (0x86b694) and CreateEmitter (0x86ca08). It is not in the base cursor class (it lives in each cursor class), so those three rows stay partial until the owner header carries it.

vox::TransitionRule (native_containers.hpp): +0x1c is a float, read as *(float*)(rule+0x1c) by UpdateOldSegmentState. The header declared it int32; this pass changed it to float (small edit, no other reader found). +0x04 (type_) is the switch kind used by UpdateOldSegmentState; +0x00 (kind_) is not read there.
